claim: Impedance-control-aware task segmentation combined with prior-guided multi-objective Bayesian optimization can learn phase-wise constant diagonal stiffness policies exposing a task-performance–compliance Pareto trade-off; reported Wipe and Door simulations achieved higher final hypervolume than tested ablations, while real-robot support was qualitative and no formal interaction stability or safety was established.
problem_and_setting: Learning compliant stiffness from demonstrations while treating task success and compliance as distinct objectives, evaluated on robosuite Wipe/Door and physical Torobo Wipe.
method_or_mechanism: IC-SLD identifies task phases and a stiffness-search space from position, velocity, acceleration and force demonstrations. Multi-objective BO searches phase-wise constant diagonal stiffness using IC-SLD parameters as pi-BO priors. High-level processing runs at 20 Hz and internal feedback about 1 kHz.
content_summary: Ten random-seed trials per simulation setting show highest n=100 hypervolume for IC-SLD+piBO. Wipe values were 618.58±18.49 versus 593.98±22.67 IC-SLD no prior, 590.04±22.74/592.40±22.76 GMM, and 596.31±38.38/595.12±14.75 SLD. Door values were 955.92±68.54 versus 923.05±82.57, 675.97±319.80/638.04±290.82 and 904.02±131.36/902.80±103.24. Door low-stiffness theta1 failed; higher-stiffness theta2/3 succeeded. Real Torobo Wipe qualitatively favored IC-SLD but lacked equivalent repeated statistics. About 100 trials or one hour were required.
synthesis_role: Primary evidence for demonstration-driven, multi-objective stiffness learning and for the distinction between compliance objectives and verified safety.
development_link: Makes segmentation impedance-aware and uses inferred dynamics as BO priors for task-compliance trade-off search.

evidence.finding: IC-SLD+piBO achieved 618.58±18.49 hypervolume at n=100, higher than tested ablations.
IC-SLD+piBO achieved 955.92±68.54, higher than tested ablations.
Each setting used 10 random seeds with means and standard deviations.
Low-stiffness theta1 failed to open the door; theta2/3 succeeded, showing a compliance-performance trade-off.
M=2 Wipe and M=3 Door performed best; too many/few segments hurt, and excessive prior strength can trap a local optimum.
IC-SLD qualitatively produced a better Pareto set than GMM; higher stiffness reduced z-axis oscillation.
Convergence required about 100 trials or one hour.

boundary_conditions: Stiffness is diagonal and phase-wise constant.
Segment count M is manually specified.
Only simulation Wipe/Door and one physical Wipe were tested.
Task reward and compliance proxy are not direct safety measures.
assumptions: Demonstrations identify useful phases and priors.

reported: Strong priors can cause local optima.
M is manual and nondiagonal stiffness raises dimensionality.
inferred: Compliance proxies do not prove physical safety.
No formal stability, passivity, force-limit or collision guarantee is established.
Physical evidence is weaker than simulation.
On-robot BO can expose hardware/users before finding a suitable policy.
